In spring, growth is the most important thing for plants. Warm sunlight and abundant rain give plants the power to break through the soil. At this time, nature is filled with the sound of life growing.

"Wake up, little dormouse!" they called happily, "Spring is here!"

在角落里，成年人会以为他不见了，其实，他还是常常会出现，会给成年人快乐，给

page_text_en:
Sky Book
I always laugh when I read picture books.
I'm not a child anymore, so why do I laugh?
This is exactly why these picture books are worth reading for children.
A picture book meant for children, which makes an adult who is no longer a child laugh, means that it makes the child still hiding inside that adult laugh. Inside an adult's heart, there is a child who never grows up. But as people grow older, this child gradually shrinks and hides deeper in the corners of their heart. Adults often think the child has disappeared. In reality, he still appears from time to time, bringing joy, innocence, childish sorrow and satisfaction, and even a bit of mischief and stubbornness to adults. But adults rarely think about why these childhood feelings and sensations resurface. They don't have time to explore the reasons. So I try to tell you: it's that child inside!
A book or story that can make the child inside a grown-up laugh means that the 'laughter,' 'cuteness,' 'wisdom,' and even what we call 'poetry' in the story are alive, not just one-time gimmicks or plastic bags.
I laugh, and you laugh too, naturally, because of the images in these books—their cute shapes, cute faces, cute mouths, cute eyes and noses, cute rolling, cute crawling, cute flying, and everything cute about them. Letting a child see these cutenesses, letting them embrace cuteness with cuteness, has the greatest meaning: it's not just about liking one book, but about liking one book after another, loving reading again and again, and eventually loving fairy tales, literature, and reading for life.
Cute picture books can give children a lifelong love for reading and reading habits. So we should deeply appreciate their inventors, writers and illustrators, publishers, and advocates.
I remember two stories from these books: one about an owl, and one about a hedgehog. The little hedgehog followed his mother to look for food, but got lost. He started searching for his mother, and when he finally found her, he had collected a lot of food on his body and spines. He hadn't expected that, and his mother certainly hadn't imagined it either.
As our children read these stories, reading them again and again, their hearts will gain much nourishment and food. They might even gain a sun, a moon, many stars, and a wonderful spring. This is something they don't realize now, and their parents might not expect either, but it's true! Just like that little owl, they have actually started to fly, even if they don't know it themselves. Gradually, gradually, they truly fly up to the high sky. When we finally look up, we suddenly realize: wow, how high!
At that moment, we can't help but feel joyful. Then we understand: those books we once read can make life soar. Those books are the sky.
Professor of Children's Literature
Author Mei Zihan
★ Mark Ezra:
Mark is an award-winning writer who has directed several feature films and is also a prolific screenwriter. He has been dedicated to writing children's books and is currently writing his first novel, frequently traveling between London and Venice.
★ Gavin Rowe:
Gavin is an outstanding picture book author who studied at Croydon Art College and Kensington Art College. He served as an art director for a major advertising company for many years and now teaches illustration and drawing at several UK universities. Gavin is married and lives in southern England with his daughter. As a freelance artist with rich experience, he has illustrated and designed covers for children's books for many years and also works in children's television programs.
★ Ren Rongrong:
A renowned Chinese translator and children's literature writer.
